text:
emma: Trying to run the quickstart sample in our ephemeral GH Actions runner. After installing redwoodctl the login step dies when it tries to save the profile. Noticed change after updating distro package.

emma: CLI output: 
```
error: could not persist profile: permission denied: /github/workspace/.config/redwood/profiles.json
failed to replace file atomically: permission denied
exit status 1
```

tony: Same. In our runners the repo is checked out as root-owned, runner job executes as runner user, so HOME/.config ends up unwritable. We usually work around by exporting XDG_CONFIG_HOME to /tmp or writing token file manually.

emma: Workaround: `mkdir -p /tmp/rwcfg && export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/tmp/rwcfg && redwoodctl login --profile ci` — works but is ugly.

lee: Two separate DX pain points here: (A) atomic rename strategy fails inside shared mounts with differing ownership; (B) device-code auth TTL (60s) is too short for workshop/demo flows and CI humans. When TTL expires the CLI exits and no clear retry command is provided.

nico: Proposal: detect EACCES on config write and print a one-line remediation with exact env var and sample command. Also automatically fall back to non-atomic safe write when running in CI-like envs (CI=1, GITHUB_ACTIONS, CI_SERVER). Add flags: `--profile-path` to explicitly write somewhere else and `--in-memory` to avoid writes and echo a token path you can persist later.

emma: Another request: have redwoodctl print the device URL as a clickable hyperlink (TERM supports it) and extend TTL when it detects human-interactive terminals. For headless runners provide `--headless-token /path` so CI can place a pre-authorized token.

tony: Is there an easy unit test we can add? Simulate open/rename returning EACCES and assert that we show the XDG suggestion.

nico: Yep I'll add a small test harness and GH issue. I'll also update docs with a recipe: "CI quickstart: export XDG_CONFIG_HOME or use --in-memory then `redwoodctl persist --path /tmp/token`".

ci-bot: (automated) failed workflow: onboarding-quickstart  auth: write permission to config. See https://ci.internal/runs/789

emma: Leaving a tiny Dockerfile and run script in devex/onboarding-repros. Repro Dockerfile: 
```
FROM debian:12
RUN useradd -m -u 101 runner
USER runner
WORKDIR /workspace
COPY . /workspace
ENV HOME=/home/runner
CMD ["/bin/sh","-c","redwoodctl login --profile ci"]
```

lee: TL;DR: onboarding broken in some container/CI setups due to atomic write + ownership mismatch; short device TTL compounds flakiness. Short-term: export XDG_CONFIG_HOME. Medium-term: CLI should detect unwritable config, fallback to safe write or in-memory profile, and add headless token flags.
